 Assets
 Sole ownership of a rental property located in Richmond, British Columbia
 Waiver Granted Pursuant to Section 39
 In accordance with section 39 of the Conflict of Interest Act (Act), Ms. Annette Anselm, former Member of the Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada (IRB), has been granted a waiver of her limitation period under section 36 insofar as it relates to entering into a contract of service with the IRB.
Ms. Anselm applied for a waiver of the period that applies to former reporting public office holders for one year following the last day in office. The waiver of the limitation period allows Ms. Anselm to enter into a contract of service with the IRB. 
In reviewing Ms. Anselm’s request, I considered all relevant factors listed under subsection 39(3) of the Act, which includes the following:
The general employment prospects of the reporting public office holder or former reporting public office holder
- Ms. Anselm has a specialty in the area which is very specific to the administration of refugee law. 
The nature and significance to the Government of Canada of the information possessed by the former reporting public office holder by virtue of that office holder’s public office
- Ms. Anselm has earned knowledge during her mandate that will continue to benefit the IRB. 
In light of the above, I have determined that the public interest in granting the waiver in relation to a contract of service to Ms. Anselm with the IRB outweighs the public interest in maintaining the prohibition. I have therefore agreed to waive the limitation period for this contract.
All other post-employment obligations under the Act continue to apply, including the prohibition on contracting or accepting employment or an appointment to a board position with any other entity set out in subsection 35(1) as well as the prohibition on making any other representations within the meaning of subsection 35(2), for the remainder of Ms. Anselm’s limitation period.
